_comment: Next Bar T0 surface. Until this file existed, tier-classify.mjs fell back to
the generic defaults, which declare NO T0 globs at all — so migrations and the
account-deletion path both classified T1 and the T0 gate could never fire.
Every T0 rule below must match at least one real file; run
because a dead T0 glob silently leaves a path unprotected.
escalate_min_t0_files was 5 until 2026-07-31. That was indefensible here: ONE
migration file is already irreversible without a restore, and restore capability
is UNVERIFIED. A change touching four T0 files would not have escalated. Now 1.
Rules resolve to the HIGHEST matching tier, not first- or last-match, so a
stricter rule always wins and rule order does not matter.
Glob the code that PERFORMS a destructive act, not just its entry point:
prune-orphan-photos.mjs was T0 while scripts/lib/photoFiles.mjs — which holds
the actual unlink loop — was T1, a gate you escape by refactoring.

rules.note: Schema and grants against live user data. Applying one is irreversible without a restore, and 0034-style grant changes can lock every user out of their own rows. Attended window only.
Fresh-project bootstrap schema — same blast radius as a migration.

Destructive and irreversible: deletes an auth user and cascades through every table they own. NOTE: this used to claim it was 'the one route holding the service-role key'. That was FALSE — src/app/api/event/route.ts also constructs a service-role client. Corrected 2026-07-31 after a review panel caught it.

The SECOND service-role route. Bypasses RLS, and is triggerable by an unauthenticated POST — the allowlist on the event name is the only control. Missed on the first pass because the map's own note asserted account/delete was the only service-role holder.
Executes a chosen migration as raw SQL against DATABASE_URL. Same blast radius as apply-migrations.ts, which was already T0 — this sibling was simply not globbed.
Sets ANY user's password via the Supabase admin API and confirms their email, bypassing the email flow entirely. That is account takeover as a supported operator tool.

Holds the actual unlink loop behind prune-orphan-photos. The wrapper was T0 while the code that does the deleting was T1 — a gate you escape by refactoring. Glob the code that performs the destructive act, not only its entry point.

Calls billable Google Places APIs across the catalog. Proposed as T0 and DEMOTED to T1 on adjudication: T0 in this map means irreversible destruction or takeover with no undo. A runaway bill is bounded, self-limiting (quotas, budget alerts) and recoverable; a dropped table with an unverified restore is not. Putting cost in the same tier devalues the label for the changes that can actually end the project. FOLLOW-UP, not fixed here: the script issues API requests BEFORE the --apply guard, so a dry run still spends. That is a one-line correctness bug and wants a MAX_CALLS cap — fixing it is the right control, not tier weight.

NOT documentation, despite the .md extension: these are the operating instructions the coding agent follows for this repository. A change here can tell the agent to skip a gate, so it must never inherit the blanket **/*.md T2. Rules resolve to the HIGHEST matching tier, so this overrides that glob.
Runs BEFORE every matched route handler, so no per-route control can gate it. A wrong matcher is an un-gateable amplification lever (C2 F1b).
The runner that applies schema changes to a live database, including the drift check that refuses an edited-after-apply file.
DELETES FILES. Backed by a backup step, but an over-broad orphan set destroys live venue media.
Rate limiting for every public route. Not T0 — it cannot destroy data — but a regression here removes the only abuse control the public surface has.

Workflow files are NOT skippable config. A workflow edit can delete the secret-scan step, widen permissions, or add a step that reads deployment secrets — i.e. it can disable the very gates protecting everything else. T1 so it is always reviewed. (Raised in operator review 2026-07-30; it was inherited as T2 from the generic defaults.)
